descriptionChirho: Core sense of physical movement toward the speaker or a destination, including arrival. Covers all tenses, persons, moods, and participial forms where the basic meaning is 'come' or 'arrive.' Arabic uses the root j-'-' (جَاءَ / يَأْتِي), Korean 오다 (oda), Swahili -kuja / -fika, Spanish venir / llegar, Hindi aana (आना). This is the overwhelmingly dominant sense of erchomai in the NT.

Substantivized present participle used as a messianic or eschatological title designating 'the one who comes / the Coming One.' Arabic uses the definite participle الآتي (al-aatii), Korean 오실 분 / 오시는 분 (the honorable one who comes), Hindi आनेवाला (aanewaalaa), Spanish 'el que viene / que-viene.' Distinct from the general participial 'coming' because it functions as a noun phrase identifying a person.

Imperative command meaning 'come here!' as a summons or invitation. Arabic distinctively uses the separate verb تَعَالَ (ta'aala, 'come hither'), a different root from the indicative j-'-' (جَاءَ), confirming this as a lexically distinct usage pattern. Korean 오라 (ora), Swahili Njoo / Njooni, Spanish Ven / Venid, Hindi आ / आओ (aa / aao).

Contextual sense where erchomai means 'enter' or 'go into' a place. Arabic uses the distinct root d-kh-l (دَخَلَ / دُخُول / تَدْخُلُوا, 'enter'), Korean 들어가다 (deureogada, 'go into'), Swahili -ingia ('enter'), Spanish entrar / entréis. The convergent cross-linguistic shift to 'enter' across unrelated language families confirms genuine polysemy.

Sense where erchomai functions as 'go' (movement away from speaker or general locomotion), contrasting with the core 'come toward' sense. Korean uses 가다 (gada, 'go') instead of 오다 (oda, 'come'), Spanish uses ir / fue / Vamos ('go'), Hindi uses गया (gayaa, 'went'). Arabic context also diverges (كَانَ يَكْرِزُ, 'was preaching' = went about preaching).

Attributive or adjectival use meaning 'coming, next, future, approaching' in a temporal sense, modifying a time word or abstract noun (e.g., 'the coming age,' 'things to come'). Spanish uses venidero / venidera / siguiente ('next, forthcoming'), Arabic الآتِي (al-aatii, temporal), Korean 다가오는 (dagaoneun, 'approaching') and 올 것들을 ('things that will come'), Swahili -jayo / yajayo ('coming/next'), Hindi आनेवाली बातें ('coming things').
